big_rules.title: Amal's spelling is the only spelling
big_rules.text: Every Arabic word is spelled the way Amal spells it: first how she types it, then her Doc's Arabizi, then her Arabic script; never a made-up spelling.

big_rules.title: Raw transcripts are never edited
big_rules.text: The transcript the machine writes is never changed; fixes are kept in a separate layer on top.

big_rules.title: A slip is only a slip when there is a signal
big_rules.text: A grammar slip counts only when there is a signal: Amal corrects or re-says it, or you ask about it.

big_rules.title: Pronunciation is never a missed word
big_rules.text: Saying a word with a wrong sound (like a dropped ع or ط) is a pronunciation note: it never counts as a missed word and never lowers the word's score.

big_rules.title: Pauses are not errors
big_rules.text: Pauses are not mistakes: a long pause and then the right answer is a right answer.

big_rules.title: Every correction becomes a rule
big_rules.text: Every correction becomes a rule: fix that one moment, and write the general rule where the next lesson will meet it, listed in the rule list.

big_rules.title: A page is never older than its source
big_rules.text: A page is never older than its data: when a newer lesson exists the page says so, and the publish check warns if a lesson is missing from the site, Amal's answers were not checked for 2 hours, or publishing has been stuck for 6 hours.
